tool_arguments.query: AWS AI workload contribution revenue percentage Q2 2026

events.content: AWS AI workload contribution revenue percentage Q2 2026

- **AWS growth:** AWS revenue was **$42.2 billion in Q2 2026**, up **36.7% year over year**—its fastest growth in 18 quarters—and Amazon said the business reached a **$169 billion annualized revenue run rate**. [[1]]

- **AI-revenue disclosure:** Amazon said AWS’s **AI business exceeded a $25 billion annual revenue run rate** and was growing at a **triple-digit year-over-year rate**; this equates to more than **$6.25 billion on a simple quarterly run-rate basis** and at least roughly **15% of AWS’s $169 billion annualized revenue**, although Amazon did not formally disclose quarterly AI revenue or its precise share of AWS growth. [[1]]

- **Management’s key comment on workload contribution:** Andy Jassy said AWS was seeing strong growth in both **AI** and **non-AI (“core”)** workloads, with each supporting the other rather than AI being an isolated revenue stream. [[2]]

- **Mechanism:** Management said AI adoption encourages customers to move to AWS and increases core-service consumption; moreover, post-training reinforcement learning and AI-agent tool use are largely CPU-intensive, benefiting AWS core compute as well as AI accelerators. [[3]]

- **Important caveat:** Therefore, it would be inaccurate to attribute all—or a defined portion—of the 36.7% AWS growth rate to AI: Amazon disclosed rapid AI revenue growth, but **did not quantify AI’s percentage-point contribution** to Q2 AWS growth. [[3, 1]]

Sources:
[S5.1] Amazon.com, Inc. - Amazon.com Announces Second Quarter Results — https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Second-Quarter-Results/

tool_arguments.query: Microsoft Azure Q2 2026 revenue growth AI contribution

events.content: Microsoft Azure Q2 2026 revenue growth AI contribution

Microsoft’s latest reported quarter was fiscal Q2 2026, ended December 31, 2025 and released January 28, 2026. [[1]]

- **Azure growth:** Azure and other cloud services revenue grew **39% year over year**, or **38% in constant currency**, versus **40% reported / 39% constant currency** in fiscal Q1 2026. [[1]] [[2]]
- **AI contribution:** Microsoft did **not disclose a separate AI percentage-point contribution** to Azure’s 39% growth in its Q2 materials. It said Azure growth was driven by demand across its services portfolio and continued growth across all workloads, while defining Azure and other cloud services as including cloud and AI consumption-based services. [[3]] [[4]]
- **Broader cloud results:** Intelligent Cloud revenue was **$32.9 billion**, up **29%** year over year, and Microsoft Cloud revenue reached **$51.5 billion**, up **26%**. [[5]]
- **AI demand and constraints:** Management said demand continued to exceed available supply, and noted that efficiency gains in its fungible fleet allowed capacity to be reallocated to monetized Azure demand during the quarter. [[5]]
- **Profitability implication:** Microsoft said Microsoft Cloud gross margin was **67%**, with the year-over-year decline reflecting continuing AI-infrastructure investment and increased AI-product usage, partly offset by Azure and Microsoft 365 efficiency gains. [[5]] 

In short, Azure expanded at a still-exceptional **39% reported growth rate**, but decelerated modestly from Q1; AI is clearly embedded in the growth narrative and infrastructure spending, yet Microsoft did not provide the precise “AI contribution” figure it had disclosed in some earlier periods. [[2]] [[6]]
